_comment: The words on each mod's feature vote page. scripts/vote-page-lib.js builds every
public/mods/ffxiv/<mod>/vote/index.html from these and one template, so the pages
differ only here. lede_html is trusted HTML written in this repository; every other
field is text and is escaped. The ideas themselves are data/catalogue.json (Ghostty)
and data/catalogues/<mod>.json; the page paths are src/lib.js VOTE_MODS.

ghostty.name: Ghostty
ghostty.title: Ghostty FFXIV Vote
ghostty.description: Vote on what the Ghostty for FFXIV terminal plugin should do next.
ghostty.lede_html: Ghostty for FFXIV is a plugin that puts a real Ghostty terminal inside Final Fantasy XIV, made by Johnneylee Jack Rollins (github.com/Spaceghost). These are ideas for what it could do next. Each was checked against how the plugin actually works: how feasible it is, how much effort it takes, and whether it stays client-side and within the game's terms of service.
ghostty.suggest_title: A split-flap board at the Gold Saucer for my CI
ghostty.suggest_detail: Describe the moment you'd want in game.

xivmcp.name: XivMcp
xivmcp.title: XivMcp Vote
xivmcp.description: Vote on what XivMcp, the MCP server inside Final Fantasy XIV, should let AI clients do next.
xivmcp.h1_before: What should your AI be able to
xivmcp.lede_html: XivMcp is a Model Context Protocol server inside Final Fantasy XIV, made by Johnneylee Jack Rollins (github.com/Spaceghost). AI clients read game state and game data over loopback, and anything that changes your game waits for your approval in game. These are ideas for what it could do next, each checked against how the plugin works and against its hard lines: client-side, your own character only, and nothing that plays the game for you.
xivmcp.suggest_title: A tool that reads my retainers' sale history
xivmcp.suggest_detail: What would you ask your AI, and what should it be able to see or do?

xivdesktop.name: XivDesktop
xivdesktop.title: XivDesktop Vote
xivdesktop.description: Vote on what XivDesktop, your Linux desktop inside Final Fantasy XIV, should do next.
xivdesktop.lede_html: XivDesktop brings your Linux desktop into Final Fantasy XIV: a keyboard-first launcher, nine workspaces and a taskbar for real application windows shown as panels in the world, on top of Ghostty. Made by Johnneylee Jack Rollins (github.com/Spaceghost). These are ideas for what it could do next, each checked against how it actually works: how feasible it is, how much effort it takes, and whether it stays client-side.
xivdesktop.suggest_title: Drag a file from my file manager onto a housing wall
xivdesktop.suggest_detail: Describe the moment you'd want in game.

xivarcade.name: XivArcade
xivarcade.title: XivArcade Vote
xivarcade.description: Vote on what XivArcade, your own classic games inside Final Fantasy XIV, should do next.
xivarcade.lede_html: XivArcade is a library for the classic games you own: started in RetroArch on the Linux host, shown as panels in the world, with every save kept in step across your machines. Bring your own games; none are downloaded. Made by Johnneylee Jack Rollins (github.com/Spaceghost). These are ideas for what it could do next, each checked against how it actually works.
xivarcade.suggest_title: A cabinet in my FC house that friends can walk up to
xivarcade.suggest_detail: Describe the moment you'd want in game.

xivwayfinder.name: XivWayfinder
xivwayfinder.title: XivWayfinder Vote
xivwayfinder.description: Vote on what XivWayfinder, the soft bead and pointing glove for Final Fantasy XIV, should do next.
xivwayfinder.lede_html: XivWayfinder shows the way softly: a bead at your target and a small pointing glove at the edge of the screen, for map flags and quest steps. Made by Johnneylee Jack Rollins (github.com/Spaceghost). These are ideas for what it could do next, each checked against how it works: it only ever points, and never moves your character.
xivwayfinder.suggest_title: Point me at the next FATE in the zone
xivwayfinder.suggest_detail: Where would you want it to lead you, and how should that feel?

xivlantern.name: XivLantern
xivlantern.title: XivLantern Vote
xivlantern.description: Vote on what XivLantern, friends, chat and channels peer to peer inside Final Fantasy XIV, should do next.
xivlantern.lede_html: XivLantern is a friend list of your own inside Final Fantasy XIV, with presence, 1:1 chat and channels, peer to peer over iroh: there is no Lantern server, and nothing from the game is ever sent. Made by Johnneylee Jack Rollins (github.com/Spaceghost). These are ideas for what it could do next, each checked against how it works and against its promise to stay a separate chat that never reads the game.
xivlantern.suggest_title: Share a waymark layout with my static's channel
xivlantern.suggest_detail: Describe the moment you'd want with your friends.

xivpiano.name: XivPiano
xivpiano.title: XivPiano Vote
xivpiano.description: Vote on what XivPiano, the Pandora radio player inside Final Fantasy XIV, should do next.
xivpiano.lede_html: XivPiano plays your Pandora stations inside Final Fantasy XIV, in the tradition of pianobar, Pithos and Elpis: thumbs up and down, tired of it, why this song, and new stations from a search. It has not been heard playing in game yet. Made by Johnneylee Jack Rollins (github.com/Spaceghost). These are ideas for what it could do next, each checked against how it works and against Pandora's terms: it streams, it never keeps a song. Pandora serves the United States only, and XivPiano is not affiliated with Pandora.
xivpiano.suggest_title: Switch to my battle station when a duty starts
xivpiano.suggest_detail: When would you want the music to change, and what should it do?

almanac.name: Almanac
almanac.title: Almanac Vote
almanac.description: Vote on what Almanac, the local AI companion for Final Fantasy XIV, should do next.
almanac.lede_html: Almanac connects a model running on your own PC to Final Fantasy XIV through XivMcp's tools: a setup wizard that reads your GPU, an in-game chat with threads, and a benchmark you can share. No cloud, no Python. Made by Johnneylee Jack Rollins (github.com/Spaceghost). These are ideas for what it could do next, each checked against how it works and whether it fits beside the game on one GPU.
almanac.suggest_title: Remember what I asked last session
almanac.suggest_detail: What would you want to ask it, and what should it know?
